items.title: Abbott to spin off its global Nutrition business as an independent listed company
items.summary: Abbott plans a tax-free spin-off of Nutrition (Ensure, Glucerna, PediaSure, Pedialyte, Similac): about $8.5bn sales, 16,000 staff, 14 plants. CEO-designate Daniel Salvadori. Abbott keeps devices, Libre, diagnostics and established medicines (about $42bn).

items.title: First needle-free adrenaline treatment for young children launched in the UK
items.summary: The first needle-free adrenaline treatment for young children is now available in the UK. The 1mg nasal spray was launched on Tuesday (20 October) and is available for the emergency treatment of anaphylaxis in young children aged 4 years and over who weigh 15 kg to less than 30 kg. The announcement comes after the...

items.title: GPs given new legal duties to proactively share information for child safeguarding
items.summary: GPs are now legally required to proactively share information about children with other safeguarding organisations where there are concerns about their welfare, even if they are not yet at risk of harm.

items.title: Nurses helping orphaned children of colleagues stay in education
items.summary: Hundreds of orphaned daughters of nurses living in developing countries have been able to access education thanks to a charity's nurse mentorship scheme and funding.

items.title: Framework for the supply of Adult and Paediatric Nutrition Products
items.summary: University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHS Foundation Trust. The East Midlands Pharmacy Collaborative (EMPC) as the Authority wishes to establish a multi-provider Framework Agreement for its members the supply of Adult and Paediatric Nutrition products as defined in this specification.

items.title: Thistle Help raises over £1,700 for children’s charity with annual showroom coffee morning

items.title: Sharp rise in year-long community care waits for children
items.summary: More than one in four children on waiting lists for community health services in England have been waiting at least a year for treatment, according to new analysis by The King’s Fund. The think tank found that 86,000 children had been waiting for 52 weeks or longer in July 2026, accounting for 27% of those...

items.title: A guide to common childhood illnesses: threadworm
items.summary: Threadworm (enterobiasis) is the most common parasitic worm infection in the UK, particularly affecting primary school-aged children. Transmission occurs via the faecal–oral route following ingestion of microscopic eggs, which can survive on surfaces for up to 2 weeks.

items.title: Children’s health at ‘crisis point’ from public health nurse shortage
items.summary: School and public health nurses have been “hollowed out” from England's health services, putting children’s health at risk from a lack of preventative healthcare, a new report has found.

items.title: School nurse workforce falls by almost 40% since 2010, analysis reveals
items.summary: The school nursing workforce has dropped by more than 1,100 professionals in England since 2010, according to a new analysis which has prompted fresh concerns around the preventative and early care that children are missing out on.

items.title: Vaping at home increases children’s asthma risk
items.summary: Children exposed to vaping at home are at increased risk of asthma flare-ups, according to new research.

items.title: Vomiting in infants: when is it reflux, and when should we worry?
items.summary: Dilemmas in paediatrics: GPwER in paediatrics Dr David Capehorn discusses how to assess the vomiting infant, and distinguish normal physiology, overfeeding and milk allergy from the rare scenarios where a child needs urgent referral Note cases discussed in this article are hypothetical and created for educational…

items.title: Infant feeding and mental health support to be rolled out across England by 2028
items.summary: A ‘Healthy Babies’ programme like what used to be provided in Sure Start centres will be rolled out to all local authorities by 2028, the Government has announced.

items.title: Implementing Benedict’s law: guidance from a school nurse
items.summary: Following the launch of new statutory allergy safety guidance this month, all state-maintained schools, academies and free schools are expected to meet a number of requirements relating to staff allergy training and allergy safety policies, among other things.

items.title: Children as young as 13 seen by NHS for bladder damage caused by ketamine
items.summary: Children as young as 13 for bladder problems associated with ketamine use according to doctors who set up an NHS clinic to manage the problem.

items.title: Provisional childhood vaccine coverage in England: July 2026
items.summary: UKHSA's monthly provisional estimates from GP data for MMRV, rotavirus, MenB, the 6-in-1 and the dTaP/IPV booster in July 2026. Supplements the official COVER statistics to give immunisation teams more timely figures; local authority figures vary because cohorts are small.

items.title: Childhood vaccination coverage (COVER) April to June 2026: 12-month coverage slips
items.summary: UKHSA's COVER data for Q1 2026/27: in England 12-month coverage fell to 89.2% for the 6-in-1, 89.5% for PCV1 and 87.6% for rotavirus, while MenB rose to 91.4%. Coverage stays below its 10-year peaks and is lowest in London and deprived areas.

items.title: Pertussis in England: 71 confirmed cases in January to March 2026
items.summary: UKHSA confirmed 71 whooping cough cases in Q1 2026, similar to Q4 2025 (77) and far below Q1 2025 (328), as the 2024 cyclical peak continues to recede. 79% were aged 15 or over; 3 were infants, one under 3 months. Infant under-3-month cases fell from 433 in 2024 to 12 in 2025.
